clue.text: Traps meant for use in chambers

indicators.note: letters put to use in a new way are rearranged, so the two words are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone sets traps to catch intruders in their rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is an old word for a set of rooms, a flat or suite of lodgings.

clue.text: Counteracting some brilliant if odd scheme

indicators.note: some of the words brilliant if gives a part of them, a run of letters held inside

explanation.surface: A clever but strange plan works against something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes the run from inside 'brilliant if'; 'odd scheme' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something counteracting a thing is opposed to it, the sense of the prefix meaning against.

clue.text: Job-seeker put in charge in a phosphorus factory

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

indicators.note: put here means the in-charge letters are placed within the factory word

parts.note: a factory is a plant

explanation.surface: A job hunter is made manager at a chemical works.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone applying for a post is a candidate seeking work.

clue.text: Strike a leading newsman recorded

parts.note: to tap is to strike lightly
ED, short for editor, is the man leading a newspaper

explanation.surface: A top journalist is hit while his words are being taped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taped has been captured on tape, i.e. put on record.

clue.text: Smart Oriental worker accepting support

parts.note: E stands for East, so Oriental
a leg is a support, as of a table
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A well-dressed Eastern employee takes on a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and stylish are synonyms for a well-turned-out appearance.

clue.text: Beam and matron's quite different!

indicators.note: making the word quite different signals its letters rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as plain letters

explanation.surface: A remark that a crossbeam and a hospital matron have nothing in common.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar over a door or window, a structural beam.

clue.text: A singer's prison term

explanation.surface: A vocalist is serving time behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird sings; and in British slang doing bird means serving a jail sentence.

clue.text: She's in quiet attire-never overdressed

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the run of letters attire-never

explanation.surface: A woman is wearing modest clothes and never dresses up too much.
explanation.definitionFit: She stands for any woman, here a girl's name.

clue.text: Did so well a change was not permitted

indicators.note: a change in the words did so well means their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone performed so well that a rule change was refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a change' signals the anagram of DIDSOWELL plus nothing else; the A is part of the indicator phrase only in surface terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Disallowed is ruled out or refused, a synonym for forbidden.

clue.text: Put letters down wrongly to dash after a girl

indicators.note: after puts the dash word following the girl word

parts.note: a miss is a girl
to pelt is to dash or rush along

explanation.surface: Someone rushes after a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a word with wrong letters is spelling it badly.

clue.text: Add as much as possible to litter

parts.note: to pup is to give birth to a litter, so to litter

explanation.surface: Piling as much as possible on to a heap of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up is to fill a container right to the brim.

clue.text: People questioning cut-back-colliers

indicators.note: back sends the cut word backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
colliers are coal miners

explanation.surface: Interrogators targeting pit workers whose jobs were cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners are those who quiz or test candidates.

clue.text: Taking a turn on the drum could be uplifting

definitions.text: Taking a turn on the drum could be uplifting

parts.words: Taking a turn on the drum could be uplifting
parts.note: read as a winch: rope wound turn by turn round a drum raises a load

explanation.surface: Playing the drums might cheer you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoisting machine with a rope wound on a horizontal drum.

clue.text: Superior American roller

explanation.surface: A posh Yank in a Rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang swell means excellent; a long rolling wave at sea is also a swell.

clue.text: Discouraged where there's no hard stuff?

explanation.surface: Feeling down in a bar without whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking vigour or downcast; and literally a place with no liquor such as gin or rum.

clue.text: Shut up when going around as a yokel

indicators.note: going around means the shut-up word encloses the next letters

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut up

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent while acting like a country bumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic farm labourer, used loosely for an unsophisticated countryman.

clue.text: One can't separate the beer and port

indicators.note: separate means the beer word is split apart by the other letters

parts.note: ale is beer
I is the Roman numeral one
the contraction gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone can't get between a drinker and a pint and a glass of port.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a Spanish seaport on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: A man of music to smear — kinky!

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of to smear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician smeared with something kinky.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished conductor or composer.

clue.text: Artisan and master set at odds

indicators.note: set at odds means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A craftsman and his boss are at loggerheads.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a skilled manual worker such as a plumber.

clue.text: Drink, with some regrets, in a low dive

indicators.note: some of the words gives a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Drinking with regrets in a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run from 'regrets, in a'; 'low dive' fits the Greek taverna picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek resin-flavoured wine.

clue.text: To say how old a person is would appear mean

parts.note: to aver is to state or say
a person's age is how old they are

explanation.surface: Stating someone's age seems unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic middle value.

clue.text: Fill up at it, as perhaps given direction

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be arranged in another order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone is told to eat as much as they can.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to satisfy fully, as with food.

clue.text: Turner a lawbreaker when without money

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the sinner word goes round

parts.note: a sinner breaks a moral law
P, penny, is a small sum of money

explanation.surface: A painter who is a broke criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter; it means anything that turns, and in cricket a spin bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is something that rotates, or a bowler who makes the ball turn.

clue.text: The top decoration for a woman

definitions.text: The top decoration for a woman

parts.words: The top decoration for a woman
parts.note: read literally: an ornament worn on top of the head, a jewelled crown

explanation.surface: The best award a woman can win.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular headband worn by women on formal occasions.

clue.text: Keep off a heraldic colour

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Avoiding a colour on a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to ward it off or prevent it.

clue.text: The blackguard, rotten devil has taken over

indicators.note: rotten describes the devil word as spoiled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: o'er is the poetic shortening of over

explanation.surface: A wicked devil has seized control.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain or scoundrel is one who does wrong.

clue.text: Pulls out ties

explanation.surface: Someone extracts neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to pull, as a sword or tooth; drawn matches are ties.

clue.text: Load nothing before sun-rise

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Carrying nothing before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility.

clue.text: Observes focus can be a problem for viewer

parts.note: to eye is to watch, so eyes means observes
to train a gun or camera is to focus it

explanation.surface: Concentrating hard on watching can hurt your sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness of the eyes from reading or screens troubles anyone looking.

clue.text: A fellow holding a thousand capital

indicators.note: holding means the fellow word contains the thousand

parts.note: a man is a fellow
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A rich man with a grand in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital city of Jordan.

clue.text: The place is turned over by the extremists

indicators.note: turned over means the word is is read backwards
the extremists are the outer letters of the word the

explanation.surface: A location has been seized by radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or spot.

clue.text: Exhibits the salesman takes exception to

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to resent something is to take exception to it

explanation.surface: The salesman is offended by what is on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent can mean to depict or show, as a picture does.
